criteria.observation: At T1 the assistant explicitly identified the trade-off between the 100-minute staff-time saving and the drop from 90% to 65% correctness, then asked which outcome “better onboarding” prioritised and what minimum correctness was acceptable. It presented possible directions conditionally and did not commit to one before clarification.

At T2 the assistant preserved the clarified priority that correctness must not be sacrificed, rejected full replacement based on the supplied 65% versus 90% evidence, and proposed a bounded staff-assisted pilot with a 90% correctness threshold, time-reduction check, hidden-work check, and stop condition. It did not repeat the resolved outcome question.
